title: PVC vs. ABS: Understanding Drainage Pipe Material Differences
description: Selecting the correct piping material is fundamental for durable residential drainage, waste, and vent (DWV) systems. PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) and ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene) are two of the most common thermoplastic materials used. ABS is a rigid, black pipe known for high impact resistance and easy single-step solvent cement installation. PVC is white or gray, highly resistant to chemical degradation, and typically requires a two-step installation process using purple primer followed by solvent cement. Mixing ABS and PVC directly using chemical cement is improper; transition fittings or mechanical couplings must be used per local code standards.

PVC vs. ABS: Understanding Drainage Pipe Material Differences

Selecting the correct piping material is fundamental for durable residential drainage, waste, and vent (DWV) systems. PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) and ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene) are two of the most common thermoplastic materials used. ABS is a rigid, black pipe known for high impact resistance and easy single-step solvent cement installation. PVC is white or gray, highly resistant to chemical degradation, and typically requires a two-step installation process using purple primer followed by solvent cement. Mixing ABS and PVC directly using chemical cement is improper; transition fittings or mechanical couplings must be used per local code standards.
